paper_metadata.title: Train-and-Scaling the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz to Solve Portfolio Diversification

summary: The paper proposes a Train‑and‑Scale training protocol for QAOA applied to portfolio diversification mapped to Maximum Independent Set. Using SP500 correlation graphs, QAOA circuits were trained from n=6 to n=30 with depth increasing to p=54, achieving average approximation gaps below ~0.4 and maintaining gaps under ~0.5 across correlation thresholds. A QAOA‑54 parameter set was then evaluated on simulated instances up to n=100 and showed a slightly smaller empirical sampling‑complexity exponent (0.044) than simulated annealing (0.057).

experiments.description: Train-and-Scale QAOA for portfolio diversification mapped to Maximum Independent Set on SP500-derived correlation graphs, evaluated across graph sizes n=6 to n=30 and multiple correlation thresholds.

algorithm.ansatz: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz with constrained mixer for MIS
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Started from smaller-instance trained parameters; new layers inserted with zero initialization at the middle of the circuit

optimizer_settings.learning_rate_schedule: exponential decay from 0.02 to 0.002 over 64 epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One binary variable / qubit per graph vertex (asset); independent-set feasibility enforced by constrained mixer rather than penalty QUBO
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize sum_i (1 - x_i) subject to x_i x_j = 0 for all edges (v_i,v_j) in E
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constrained QAOA mixer that preserves the independent-set subspace; no penalty term reported
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: C_mis = sum_(v_i,v_j in E) σ1_i σ1_j; cost Hamiltonian H_c = sum_i σ0_i

problem_instance.description: Portfolio diversification on SP500 assets via correlation-threshold graphs; graphs generated by breadth-first search around a randomly selected starting node from monthly SP500 correlation graphs

dataset_specification.description: Public Kaggle stock-market dataset; after cleaning, between 350 and 500 stocks per month; survivorship bias noted

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily returns computed from prices; monthly average returns and Pearson correlations estimated; correlation threshold λ used to build unweighted graph with edge if |C_ij| > λ; subgraphs generated by BFS around a random starting node
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Approximation gap and success probability/sampling complexity reported over 500 graphs per size; training used 64 epochs and repeated retraining while scaling depth and instance size

implementation_details.classical_solver: parameter-shift gradient descent; simulated annealing used only as classical baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Graph construction from correlation thresholding; BFS subgraph extraction; random partitioning of mixer generators into commuting groups
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation gap and success probability computed from sampled bitstrings

speedup_claims.conditions: sampling-complexity comparison for portfolio diversification instances with λ = 0.1, n = 6 to 100, using QAOA trained up to p = 54
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports a smaller fitted scaling exponent for QAOA than simulated annealing, but does not claim a formal asymptotic speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial scaling in depth and sampling complexity
speedup_claims.conditions: if the observed trend continues to hundreds of variables
speedup_claims.caveats: Described as a possibility, not proven.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly characterized; paper discusses p-depth scaling empirically as O(n) for tested instances

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not quantified; current experiments simulate up to ~100 qubits with depth p=54 and require ~2^17 gradient updates for training.
limiting_factors: Experiments performed entirely in classical simulation
Classical simulated annealing baseline used only for empirical scaling comparison
Training cost of variational circuits scales heavily with gradient evaluations
Circuit depth grows roughly linearly with problem size (p≈2n during training)

notes: No specific quantum hardware or simulator is named; hardware.type left not_specified.
num_qubits inferred from n=30 maximum instance size and one qubit per binary variable in MIS encoding.
num_variational_params inferred as 2p for QAOA with p=54, giving 108 parameters.
